Farid is at the gym (G).
Olivia is at the campground (C).
Devika is at the barbershop (BS).

Emily is at the library (L).
Isabella is at the zoo (Z).

S4: Person at O says Person at C tells the truth. ($T(O) \iff T(C)$)
S5: Person at M says Person at BG lies. ($T(M) \iff L(BG)$)
S6: Person at V says Person at F lies. ($T(V) \iff L(F)$)
S7: Person at L says Person at M lies. ($T(L) \iff L(M)$)
S8: Person at C says Person at V tells the truth. ($T(C) \iff T(V)$)
S9: Person at G says Person at Z lies. ($T(G) \iff L(Z)$)
S10: Person at Z says Person at B tells the truth. ($T(Z) \iff T(B)$)
S11: Person at M says Person at O tells the truth. ($T(M) \iff T(O)$)

We also have some external information:
E1: Person at F saw a firetruck. (This is an observation, not a statement about truth/lie status, but it might be relevant if we assume truth-tellers report facts truthfully, which is standard).
E2: Person at B saw a firetruck.
E3: Person at G thinks their friend is lying. (This is an internal thought, usually not used unless specified how it relates to truth-telling).

   $L(F)$ is true.

   The person at the vineyard (Priya) tells the truth. $T(V)$.

3. Using S8: $T(C) \iff T(V)$. Since $T(V)$ is true, $T(C)$ must be true.
   The person at the campground (Olivia) tells the truth. $T(C)$.

4. Using S4: $T(O) \iff T(C)$. Since $T(C)$ is true, $T(O)$ must be true.
   The person at the observatory (Ryan) tells the truth. $T(O)$.

5. Using S11: $T(M) \iff T(O)$. Since $T(O)$ is true, $T(M)$ must be true.
   The person at the museum (Grace) tells the truth. $T(M)$.

6. Using S5: $T(M) \iff L(BG)$. Since $T(M)$ is true, $L(BG)$ must be true.
   The person at the botanical garden (Ethan) lies. $L(BG)$.

7. Using S7: $T(L) \iff L(M)$. Since $T(M)$ is true, $L(M)$ is false. Therefore, $T(L)$ must be false.
   The person at the library (Emily) lies. $L(L)$.

8. Using S2: $T(B) \iff L(L)$. Since $L(L)$ is true, $T(B)$ must be true.
   The person at the bookstore (Zara) tells the truth. $T(B)$.

9. Using S10: $T(Z) \iff T(B)$. Since $T(B)$ is true, $T(Z)$ must be true.
   The person at the zoo (Isabella) tells the truth. $T(Z)$.

10. Using S1: $T(BS) \iff T(Z)$. Since $T(Z)$ is true, $T(BS)$ must be true.
    The person at the barbershop (Devika) tells the truth. $T(BS)$.

11. Using S9: $T(G) \iff L(Z)$. Since $T(Z)$ is true, $L(Z)$ is false. Therefore, $T(G)$ must be false.
    The person at the gym (Farid) lies. $L(G)$.

We have determined the truthfulness of all required parties:
Person at the gym (Farid): Lies ($L(G)$).
Person at the zoo (Isabella): Tells the truth ($T(Z)$).
Person at the bookstore (Zara): Tells the truth ($T(B)$).

The question asks:
1. Does the person at the gym tell the truth? (No, $L(G)$)
2. Does the person at the zoo tell the truth? (Yes, $T(Z)$)
3. Does the person at the bookstore tell the truth? (Yes, $T(B)$)

Final Answer: no, yes, yes
